MIXED-SIGNAL: the hand-drawn analog inverter, imported as a hard macro.
tt-support-tools generates src/user_config.json and merges it OVER this
file, but only for the keys it owns (DESIGN_NAME, VERILOG_FILES, DIE_AREA,
FP_DEF_TEMPLATE, VDD_PIN, GND_PIN, RT_MAX_LAYER). Everything below
survives into the LibreLane run.
Built by analog/layout/build_tt_analog_inverter.py; timing measured in
ngspice by analog/char/characterize.py. Placed by hand rather than by
the macro placer, and the numbers are not arbitrary: x sits on the site
grid (2.88 + 0.48k) and y on the row grid (3.78k), so the macro lands
flush in the rows, and x is chosen so that a whole VPWR/VGND strap pair
of the tile PDN (13.6um offset, 38.87um pitch, 4um apart) falls inside
the macro's 20.16um width, which is what gives both supplies a via.
(A '//' key is only stripped at the top level - LibreLane rejects one
inside the Macro object itself.)
Keep the placer, and every route, away from the analog block. The LEF
already blocks Metal1..Metal4 over the macro; the halo keeps standard
cells from crowding right up against the guard ring, and keeps the
PDN's own straps off it except where they are hooked on purpose.
The PDN halo stays at zero: a halo keeps the grid's straps away from
the macro, and the macro's straps have to be reachable from it.
Hook the macro's supplies to the tile PDN.
<instance_rx> <vdd_net> <gnd_net> <vdd_pin> <gnd_pin>
The macro grid vias between PDN_VERTICAL_LAYER and PDN_HORIZONTAL_LAYER.
The tile's grid is TopMetal1 (vertical) and, with FP_PDN_MULTILAYER off,
PDN_HORIZONTAL_LAYER is used for NOTHING ELSE - see pdn_cfg.tcl, where
the horizontal stripe and the core ring are both inside the multilayer
branch. Naming Metal4 here is therefore how the macro's Metal4 power
straps get vias up to the TopMetal1 grid, and it changes nothing else.
Left at its TopMetal2 default the macro grid has no layer in common with
the macro and PDN quits with PDN-0232 then PDN-0233.
